calibration_warning: The weights and band thresholds below are a defensible starting calibration, not an empirically validated model. They encode a professional judgement about relative importance and have not been fitted against outcome data. Treat the first deployment as a calibration exercise: score units, compare against practitioner judgement, and adjust. Publishing these numbers as though they were validated would be exactly the false precision the ratio critique objects to.
design_note: Transposed from the CAF-OS capability router, which scores each shot across weighted dimensions and returns a recommended engine, an alternative, rationale, risk and confidence. Here the unit of analysis is a business unit and the recommendation is a coverage model. Headcount enters as a bounded modifier rather than a weighted dimension, which is the whole argument made structural.

dimensions.name: Change load
dimensions.definition: Concurrent organisational change the unit is absorbing: restructures, leadership transitions, system implementations, integrations, operating model shifts.

dimensions.name: Manager capability gap
dimensions.definition: Inverse of people-management capability across the unit's manager population: tenure in role, prior people-management experience, span of control, escalation frequency.

dimensions.name: Employee relations intensity
dimensions.definition: Aggregated ER case rate per 100 staff per quarter, normalised against the organisation's own distribution rather than an external benchmark.
evidence_sources: aggregated ER case counts by unit
dimensions.constraint: Unit-aggregated only. Case narratives and individual identifiers are prohibited inputs.

dimensions.name: Structural ambiguity
dimensions.definition: Unclear decision rights, matrix or dual reporting, recently redrawn boundaries, contested accountabilities.

dimensions.name: Workforce volatility
dimensions.definition: Combined hiring rate, attrition rate and contingent workforce proportion, measuring churn in the population the HRBP supports.

dimensions.name: Industrial relations load
dimensions.definition: Active consultation obligations, collective agreement coverage, statutory notification exposure.

population_modifier.method: log-scaled headcount relative to the organisation's median unit size, clamped to the range
population_modifier.rationale: Headcount is real but secondary. Capping its influence at half a point on a ten point index prevents a large stable unit from outranking a small unit in crisis, which is the failure mode the employee-to-HRBP ratio produces by construction.

bands.description: Sustained embedded HRBP coverage. Demand is high across several dimensions simultaneously.
Shared HRBP coverage across two or more units with flex capacity for peaks.
Tiered service delivery with escalation routes. Dedicated partnering is not warranted by current demand.

leakage_check.definition: Proportion of HRBP time spent on work that a shared services tier or manager self-service layer should absorb.
leakage_check.caution_text: Operational share exceeds the caution threshold. High demand here may reflect tiering leakage rather than a capacity shortfall. Adding HRBP capacity without redesigning the delivery tiers is likely to entrench the defect. Review the operating model before acting on this recommendation.
leakage_check.rationale: This is the substantive finding in most sizing reviews. Encoding it as a mandatory caveat prevents the tool from being used to justify headcount growth that a work redesign would have made unnecessary.

confidence.method: product of data completeness and freshness factors, clamped to [0.2, 0.95]
confidence.completeness: share of dimensions with evidence present
confidence.freshness: 1.0 within one quarter, 0.85 within two, 0.6 beyond two
confidence.ceiling_rationale: Confidence is capped below 1.0 because the rubric itself is provisional. A model that reports certainty about an uncalibrated instrument is misreporting.
